---

**1.0 CALL TO ORDER**

The Chair declared the meeting open at 10:05 hrs. The Chair welcomed all members and noted the presence of a quorum (9 of 11 voting members present).

---

**2.0 APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MINUTES**

The minutes of the meeting held on 1 November 2024 (FOC/2024/11-01) were circulated to members via email on 8 November 2024.

**Motion:** That the minutes of the meeting held on 1 November 2024 be approved as a true and accurate record of the proceedings.

**Moved by:** Mr. Devan Rajaratnam
**Seconded by:** Ms. Grace Lim

**Discussion:** No amendments were proposed. The Chair noted that the action items from the previous meeting would be reviewed under Agenda Item 3.0.

**Resolution:** The motion was carried unanimously.

In the minutes, the Festival Organising Committee approved_date was recorded as 2024-11-15. Record status: historical.

---

**3.0 MATTERS ARISING FROM PREVIOUS MINUTES**

**3.1 Action Item 2024/11-01-01 (Venue Booking – Main Stage Area)**
Mr. Devan Rajaratnam reported that the initial enquiry to the National Parks Board (NParks) for the use of the East Coast Park (Area E1) had been submitted. NParks has acknowledged receipt and indicated that the formal application window opens on 1 December 2024. Mr. Rajaratnam will submit the formal application on that date. He noted that the preliminary feasibility check suggested the area can accommodate an estimated 2,500 pax for the main stage, subject to final confirmation.

**3.2 Action Item 2024/11-01-02 (Budget Template Distribution)**
Ms. Amelia Wong confirmed that the revised budget template (Version 2.1) had been circulated to all department leads on 5 November 2024. She requested that all leads return their preliminary budget line items by **22 November 2024** to allow for consolidation before the next Finance Sub-Committee meeting.

---

**4.0 FINANCIAL UPDATE (FOR INFORMATION)**

Ms. Amelia Wong presented a summary of the current financial position as of 14 November 2024.

**4.1 Overall Budget Overview**

| Item | Approved Budget (SGD) | Committed / Spent (SGD) | Balance (SGD) | Remarks |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Venue & Permits | 15,000 | 1,200 | 13,800 | Deposit paid for preliminary site survey |

| Operations & Logistics | 18,000 | 2,100 | 15,900 | Includes fencing, portable toilets, signage |
| Volunteer Management | 8,000 | 900 | 7,100 | T-shirts, meals, insurance |
| Safety & Medical | 12,000 | 0 | 12,000 | Quotations pending from 2 providers |

- Mr. Marcus Tan reminded all leads that the contingency fund is strictly for unforeseen circumstances and any utilisation requires a motion and approval by the Committee.

---

**5.0 VENUE OPTIONS AND SELECTION CRITERIA**

Mr. Devan Rajaratnam presented three potential venue options for the 2025 festival, scheduled for **8 March 2025** (Saturday). The presentation included a comparative analysis based on capacity, accessibility, cost, and site conditions.
**2.0 MATTERS ARISING**

**2.1 Lead Budget Line Items**
The Chairperson noted that all leads had submitted their preliminary budget line items by the revised deadline of 22 November 2024. The consolidated figures were presented in the Financial Update at Item 4.0 below. No further action required.

**2.2 Venue Selection**
Mr. Devan Rajaratnam reported that the Committee had shortlisted two venues at the previous meeting (The Green at Marina East and the Riverside Park lawn). A site visit was conducted on 25 January 2025. The outcome of the site visit and the final selection will be discussed under Item 5.0.

---

**3.0 PROGRAMMING SCHEDULE – REVISION (FOR DECISION)**

Mr. Devan Rajaratnam presented a revision to the Programming Schedule, now designated **Programming Schedule v5**.

He explained that the revision was necessary to accommodate a confirmed international act whose management had only recently provided final performance timing requirements. The key changes in v5 are:

- Adjustment of the main stage line-up order to avoid a clash between two high-priority acts.
- Reallocation of the acoustic tent slot to a local emerging artist.
- Updated technical run-through and soundcheck times for the main stage.

**Mr. Rajaratnam noted that Programming Schedule v5 start_date was initially set to 2025-03-14. Record status: superseded.** He clarified that this was a preliminary date that had been superseded following further coordination with the venue and the technical production team. The current working date for the festival remains as previously agreed, and the schedule document will be updated accordingly once the final date is confirmed.

**Discussion:**
- Ms. Rachel Teo queried whether the change in the main stage line-up order would affect the crowd flow management plan. Mr. Rajaratnam confirmed that the Operations Sub-Committee had been consulted and that the revised order would reduce congestion near the main stage during the peak hour.
- Mr. Benjamin Koh raised a concern regarding the soundcheck times, stating that the original allocation was insufficient for the headline act's full production. He proposed that the soundcheck for the headline act be extended by 30 minutes, pushing the start of the secondary stage's soundcheck later. This was accepted by Mr. Rajaratnam and will be incorporated into a subsequent revision of the schedule.

*Resolved:* That the Committee adopts Programming Schedule v5, subject to the amendment regarding the extended soundcheck time for the headline act, and that the schedule document be updated with the final confirmed festival date.
*Proposed by:* Mr. Devan Rajaratnam
*Seconded by:* Ms. Amelia Wong
*Vote:* All in favour. Motion carried.

Ms. Amelia Wong presented the updated financial position as of 31 January 2025.

**4.1 Revised Budget Overview**

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Venue & Permits | 15,000 | 14,200 | 800 | Final payment due upon confirmation of date |
| Stage & Sound Production | 45,000 | 22,500 | 22,500 | 50% deposit paid to vendor; balance on completion |
| Artist Fees & Hospitality | 60,000 | 45,000 | 15,000 | 3 acts confirmed; 1 deposit pending |
| Marketing & Communications | 25,000 | 12,800 | 12,200 | Design retainer paid; print quotes under review |
| Operations & Logistics | 18,000 | 6,500 | 11,500 | Fencing and portable toilets confirmed |
| Volunteer Management | 8,000 | 2,400 | 5,600 | T-shirt order placed; insurance pending |

**Discussion:**
- Ms. Rachel Teo noted that the Safety & Medical budget line remained fully unspent. Ms. Faridah Hassan reported that two quotations had been received and that she would present a comparison table at the next meeting for a decision. She stated that the quotes were within the approved budget range.
- Mr. Marcus Tan reminded the Committee that any utilisation of the contingency fund would require a formal motion.
- Ms. Amelia Wong flagged that the final venue payment is dependent on the confirmation of the festival date, which is linked to the update of Programming Schedule v5.
**3.1 Confirmation of Festival Date**

Mr. Devan Rajaratnam opened the discussion by reminding the Committee that the festival date had been left pending at the previous meeting, pending confirmation from the relevant authorities regarding the use of the venue and the issuance of the necessary permits.

Ms. Amelia Wong reported that she had received verbal confirmation from the venue management earlier that day that the site would be available on the proposed date. She also noted that the application for the standard event permit had been submitted and that the processing time was estimated at two to three weeks. No objections had been raised to date.

Mr. Marcus Tan confirmed that the operations team had completed a preliminary site walk-through and that the logistics plan was viable for the proposed date.

*Resolved:* That the festival date be confirmed as 21 March 2025, subject to the receipt of the final event permit.

*Proposed by:* Ms. Amelia Wong
*Seconded by:* Mr. Marcus Tan
*Vote:* All in favour. Motion carried.

**3.2 Programming Schedule v6**

Ms. Rachel Teo presented the updated Programming Schedule v6, which had been revised to reflect the confirmed festival date. She highlighted the key changes from v5:

- The schedule now reflects the confirmed festival date of 21 March 2025.
- The headline act's soundcheck has been extended by 30 minutes, as previously agreed.
- The second stage's opening act has been swapped with the closing act on the main stage to better manage crowd flow during peak hours.
- Two volunteer shift timings have been adjusted to align with the updated stage times.

Mr. Daniel Ong noted that the stage and production team had reviewed the revised timings and found them workable. He flagged one minor concern regarding the turnaround time between the second-to-last and last acts on the main stage, which is now 20 minutes instead of the original 30 minutes. He stated that this was acceptable but would require the stage crew to be on high alert during that period.

Ms. Faridah Hassan asked whether the revised end time of the festival (23:00 hrs) had been reflected in the schedule. Ms. Rachel Teo confirmed that this had been updated in v6.

*Resolved:* That the Committee adopts Programming Schedule v6, incorporating the confirmed festival date of 21 March 2025 and the amendments discussed at the previous meeting, and that the schedule document be updated and circulated to all relevant stakeholders.

*Proposed by:* Mr. Kevin Lim
*Seconded by:* Mr. Daniel Ong
*Vote:* All in favour. Motion carried.

**Note:** Programming Schedule v6 start_date was moved to 2025-03-21. Record status: current. This is the current working schedule for the festival and supersedes all previous versions.

---

**4.0 REVIVAL ANNOUNCEMENT AND PUBLIC COMMUNICATIONS PLAN**

**4.1 Background**

Ms. Rachel Teo reminded the Committee that the festival had not been held for two years due to the pandemic and subsequent venue renovations. The decision to revive the festival this year was made at the Committee's meeting in November 2024.

**4.2 Announcement Timeline**

Ms. Rachel Teo proposed the following timeline for the public announcement:

- **13 March 2025:** Soft launch via social media (teaser posts with the festival logo and a countdown).
- **17 March 2025:** Official announcement of the festival date, venue, and first batch of confirmed acts, via press release, social media, and the community newsletter.
- **19 March 2025:** Announcement of the full lineup and ticketing details.

*Discussion:*
- Mr. Kevin Lim asked whether the announcement should be delayed until the event permit is confirmed. Ms. Amelia Wong advised that the permit was likely to be issued by mid-March, and that the announcement could proceed on 17 March as planned, with a caveat in the press release that the event is subject to permit approval.
- Mr. Marcus Tan noted that the marketing materials were largely ready and that the design retainer had already been paid.

- Reallocation of the acoustic tent slot to a local emerging artist.

**3.1 Confirmation of Festival Date**

Mr. Devan Rajaratnam opened the discussion by reminding the Committee that the festival date had been left pending at the previous meeting, pending confirmation from the relevant authorities regarding the use of the venue and the issuance of the necessary permits.

Ms. Amelia Wong reported that she had received verbal confirmation from the venue management earlier that day that the site would be available on the proposed date. She also noted that the application for the standard event permit had been submitted and that the processing time was estimated at two to three weeks. No objections had been raised to date.

Mr. Marcus Tan confirmed that the operations team had completed a preliminary site walk-through and that the logistics plan was viable for the proposed date.

*Resolved:* That the festival date be confirmed as 21 March 2025, subject to the receipt of the final event permit.

*Proposed by:* Ms. Amelia Wong
*Seconded by:* Mr. Marcus Tan
*Vote:* All in favour. Motion carried.

**3.2 Programming Schedule v6**

Ms. Rachel Teo presented the updated Programming Schedule v6, which had been revised to reflect the confirmed festival date. She highlighted the key changes from v5:

- The schedule now reflects the confirmed festival date of 21 March 2025.
- The headline act's soundcheck has been extended by 30 minutes, as previously agreed.
- The second stage's opening act has been swapped with the closing act on the main stage to better manage crowd flow during peak hours.
- Two volunteer shift timings have been adjusted to align with the updated stage times.

Mr. Daniel Ong noted that the stage and production team had reviewed the revised timings and found them workable. He flagged one minor concern regarding the turnaround time between the second-to-last and last acts on the main stage, which is now 20 minutes instead of the original 30 minutes. He stated that this was acceptable but would require the stage crew to be on high alert during that period.

Ms. Faridah Hassan asked whether the revised end time of the festival (23:00 hrs) had been reflected in the schedule. Ms. Rachel Teo confirmed that this had been updated in v6.

*Resolved:* That the Committee adopts Programming Schedule v6, incorporating the confirmed festival date of 21 March 2025 and the amendments discussed at the previous meeting, and that the schedule document be updated and circulated to all relevant stakeholders.

*Proposed by:* Mr. Kevin Lim
*Seconded by:* Mr. Daniel Ong
*Vote:* All in favour. Motion carried.

**Note:** Programming Schedule v6 start_date was moved to 2025-03-21. Record status: current. This is the current working schedule for the festival and supersedes all previous versions.

---

**4.0 REVIVAL ANNOUNCEMENT AND PUBLIC COMMUNICATIONS PLAN**

**4.1 Background**

Ms. Rachel Teo reminded the Committee that the festival had not been held for two years due to the pandemic and subsequent venue renovations. The decision to revive the festival this year was made at the Committee's meeting in November 2024.

**4.2 Announcement Timeline**

Ms. Rachel Teo proposed the following timeline for the public announcement:

- **13 March 2025:** Soft launch via social media (teaser posts with the festival logo and a countdown).
- **17 March 2025:** Official announcement of the festival date, venue, and first batch of confirmed acts, via press release, social media, and the community newsletter.
- **19 March 2025:** Announcement of the full lineup and ticketing details.

*Discussion:*
- Mr. Kevin Lim asked whether the announcement should be delayed until the event permit is confirmed. Ms. Amelia Wong advised that the permit was likely to be issued by mid-March, and that the announcement could proceed on 17 March as planned, with a caveat in the press release that the event is subject to permit approval.
- Mr. Marcus Tan noted that the marketing materials were largely ready and that the design retainer had already been paid.

ENCLOSURE 2: PERMIT CONDITIONS – EP/2025/0417 (ORIGINAL CONDITIONS, SUPERSEDED)

The following conditions apply to the conduct of the festival under Permit No. EP/2025/0417:

1. NOISE LIMITS
   1.1 The maximum permissible sound level at the boundary of the event site shall not exceed 85 dB(A) as measured over a 15-minute Leq period. This condition is based on the Site Safety Plan V3 and has been superseded by the revised limit in Enclosure 3.
   1.2 Sound level measurements shall be conducted at the four boundary monitoring points identified in the Site Safety Plan. Readings shall be logged at 15-minute intervals during all performance hours.
   1.3 The permit holder shall engage an accredited noise consultant to conduct continuous boundary monitoring. Monitoring reports shall be submitted to this office within 48 hours of the conclusion of each festival day.

2. WASTE MANAGEMENT
   2.1 The permit holder shall implement a waste segregation plan for recyclables, general waste, and food waste. A minimum of 40% of all waste generated shall be diverted from landfill.
   2.2 Adequate waste receptacles shall be provided throughout the event site, with a minimum ratio of one receptacle per 100 attendees.
   2.3 Waste collection shall occur at least twice daily, with final collection no later than one hour after the conclusion of daily programming.

3. AIR QUALITY
   3.1 No open burning of any material shall be conducted within the event site.
   3.2 All cooking equipment used by food vendors shall be approved by this office prior to the event. A list of approved equipment is attached as Annex A.
   3.3 The permit holder shall ensure that generator sets are placed at least 10 metres from any public thoroughfare and are fitted with appropriate exhaust filtration.

4. WATER MANAGEMENT
   4.1 Any discharge of water from the event site shall comply with the standards set out in the Sewerage and Drainage Act. No discharge shall occur without prior written approval.
   4.2 The permit holder shall maintain a spill response kit at the site office, containing absorbent materials sufficient for a 20-litre spill.

5. GENERAL CONDITIONS
   5.1 The permit holder shall display a copy of this permit at the main entrance of the event site throughout the festival period.
   5.2 Any request for variation of these conditions shall be submitted in writing at least 14 days prior to the event date.
   5.3 The permit holder shall ensure that all contractors and vendors are made aware of these conditions.

**RE: ADDENDUM 2 TO ENVIRONMENTAL PERMIT CONDITIONS – MERIDIAN BAY MUSIC & ARTS FESTIVAL (17–19 APRIL 2025)**

We refer to our previous correspondence dated 10 March 2025 (Permit No. EP/2025/0417) and the subsequent addendum issued on 12 March 2025. This addendum incorporates further operational details arising from the site walkthrough conducted on 13 March 2025 and supersedes the earlier addendum in its entirety.

Please note that the original permit conditions remain in full force. The following revised and additional conditions apply.

**1. NOISE MANAGEMENT – REVISED**

1.1 The overall sound level at the boundary of the event site, measured at any point along the perimeter fence line, shall not exceed 65 dB(A) Leq(5min) between the hours of 10:00 and 22:00. Between 22:00 and 23:00, the limit shall be 55 dB(A) Leq(5min). No amplified music shall be permitted after 23:00 on any day of the festival.

1.2 The permit holder shall deploy a continuous noise monitoring system at the two fixed locations identified during the site walkthrough (at the north-west corner near the marina promenade and at the south-east corner adjacent to the residential block). The monitoring system shall log data at five-minute intervals and the data shall be retained for a period of not less than three months after the conclusion of the festival.

1.3 During the site walkthrough, it was noted that the main stage orientation has been rotated 30 degrees towards the marina. This is acceptable provided that the speaker arrays are configured with a downward tilt of no less than 10 degrees. The sound engineer shall submit a written confirmation of this configuration to the undersigned no later than 15 April 2025.

1.4 Should the noise limits be exceeded, the permit holder shall take immediate remedial action, including but not limited to reducing the mix volume or adjusting the equalisation. A record of any such exceedance and the remedial action taken shall be maintained in the site logbook.

**2. WASTE MANAGEMENT – ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS**

2.1 In addition to the segregated bins specified in the original permit, the permit holder shall provide at least four (4) additional bins for aluminium can collection at high-traffic areas, namely near the main entrance, the food village, the merchandise tent, and the marina viewing deck. These bins shall be clearly labelled and shall be emptied at the same frequency as the general waste bins.

2.2 The licensed waste contractor shall provide a daily waste summary report to the site office by 09:00 each morning, indicating the total weight of general waste, recyclables, and food waste collected on the preceding day. These reports shall be made available to NEA officers upon request.

2.3 With reference to the food waste generated by the cooking oil, the grease trap servicing log shall be countersigned by the stall operator and the appointed contractor. The log shall be kept at the site office and shall be available for inspection at all times.

**3. AIR QUALITY – CLARIFICATION**

3.1 For the avoidance of doubt, the requirement in condition 3.1 of the original permit that generators be placed at least 10 metres from any food preparation area applies to all generators, including backup units that may only be used in the event of a mains power failure. Backup generators shall be tested for a maximum of 15 minutes per day during the festival period, and the test shall be recorded in the site logbook.

3.2 The permit holder is reminded that the use of charcoal grills is not permitted at any stall. Only gas-fired or electric cooking equipment shall be used. This condition was communicated verbally during the pre-event briefing on 10 March 2025 and is now confirmed in writing.
